eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Six
subtitle: Lesson 28 · Practice Sets

code:
SELECT h.je_header_id, h.name,
       SUM(l.entered_dr) AS total_debits,
       SUM(l.entered_cr) AS total_credits
FROM gl_je_headers h
INNER JOIN gl_je_lines l ON l.je_header_id = h.je_header_id
WHERE h.period_name = 'JUN-26'
GROUP BY h.je_header_id, h.name
HAVING SUM(l.entered_dr) <> SUM(l.entered_cr);
caption: Zero rows is the healthy outcome here — unlike most exception checks in this course.
The simplest query in the course — and one of the most important guardrails before processing anything.

eyebrow: "Which accounts swung the most, period over period?"
code:
WITH current_period AS (
  SELECT code_combination_id, period_net_dr-period_net_cr net_activity
  FROM gl_balances WHERE period_name='JUN-26' AND actual_flag='A'
), prior_period AS (
  SELECT code_combination_id, period_net_dr-period_net_cr net_activity
  FROM gl_balances WHERE period_name='MAY-26' AND actual_flag='A'
)
SELECT c.code_combination_id, c.net_activity, p.net_activity,
       ABS(c.net_activity - NVL(p.net_activity,0)) AS swing
FROM current_period c
LEFT OUTER JOIN prior_period p ON p.code_combination_id=c.code_combination_id
ORDER BY swing DESC FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY;
caption: ABS() treats a big swing up and a big swing down as equally worth investigating.
